correctness.rationale: For fixed completion time t and multiplicity r>=2, marking the last new coupon and one multiplicity-r coupon gives exactly m! binom(t-1,r) S(t-1-r,m-2) weighted successful sequences. Summing this coefficient identity produces the stated derivative transform. Differentiating the r=2 rational function at x=1 gives the displayed harmonic mean and covariance. The covariance sign follows from an explicit strictly positive increment for its harmonic bracket. Exhaustive sequence enumeration and exact rational replay agree with every checked identity.

value.rationale: Completion time is the defining coupon-collector stopping variable, while the exact-r multiplicity spectrum records how unevenly the already-seen types accumulated before the last discovery. The joint transform connects these two classical objects for every r>=2 and yields all mixed completion-time moments. The doubleton corollary gives a sharp finite negative-dependence law and a large-m scale of order m(log m)^2, quantifying how delayed completion shifts mass away from low multiplicities. This is a structural stopped-occupancy identity rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
